_about: What's new in each version of Manifexus, newest first. Shown in Updates. Write for people, not developers: short, plain sentences about what they can now do. The newest entry's version is what gets built and tagged; older entries can give the "commit" they were released from.

releases.headline: A fresh, calmer dashboard, and problems fixed in one tap: automatically, step by step yourself, or with a private AI.
new: A fresh, calmer dashboard. Every stack is one clean panel with its apps inside, showing at a glance whether everything is running. Tap a stack's name to fold it away.
Stack actions. Each stack's ⋯ menu can Start, Restart or Stop all its apps, edit its compose file, or open the new Stack Details screen.

Apps and their databases together. A database or cache that belongs to an app (like Nextcloud's MariaDB) no longer gets its own card. The app's icon gets a small database badge, the card warns "Database stopped" if it stops, and starting the app starts it too. Its details are inside the app's Details.
Cleaner app cards. Each card shows the app's icon, name and whether it's running, with Open, Restart and Stop right there. Moving and groups are in the ⋯ menu, and tapping a card opens its details.

Open goes straight to the app's web page. Manifexus checks each port and picks the one that is really a web page (never a peer or database port). If there are several, the arrow next to Open lists them and lets you pick the default.
Real icons and names. Manifexus finds each app's icon (from the big icon sets, the app's own web page, or its GitHub project) and uses its real name, like Usenet Ultimate instead of usenet-ultimate.
Project Page. App Details links to the app's project on GitHub and shows its latest release.
Fix This. Every problem in Diagnostics' To Fix list now has three ways to fix it: Fix Automatically, Fix It Myself or Fix with AI.

Fix Automatically. For problems Manifexus knows the answer to (a settings path without its leading /, an app listed in two stacks, an app that's stopped or unhealthy) it prepares the change itself, no AI needed. You see it first, and it's backed up and saved in Restore.
Fix It Myself. Step-by-step instructions for every problem, with the exact commands to copy and buttons for the Manifexus screens that do each step. When you're done, Check Again confirms it's fixed.
Fix with AI. For everything else, a private AI built into Manifexus looks into the problem and proposes a fix. It runs on your own server: free, private, and nothing leaves your network.
improved: Running, Stopped, Stacks and Ports now live in the header. Tap Running or Stopped to show only those apps, or Ports to see which app uses each port.
Stacks and Groups are now two big titles you tap between, with search beside them and one + button for New Stack and New Group.
Progress follows along: while a move, restore or fix runs, the screen scrolls to the step that's working (scroll up yourself and it waits for you).
Show All Steps opens every step with its commands right on top of the progress, and Back takes you straight back to it.
Each app's icon is its own: the one its page shows in the browser tab, saved the first time it's seen and used on every screen.

Fixing has its own screen. It shows the problem, works on it step by step, then shows the change with a before and after of every file: Make Changes, Do It Myself or Not Now. After the change it runs the checks again to confirm the problem is gone. One problem, start to finish.
The AI knows what Manifexus can do: when a screen does the job (Move, Restore, Settings…) it offers a button that opens it, instead of terminal steps.

The AI chooses the model for each problem by its real speed on your server: when the smarter model is about as fast, it does everything. Thinking is kept short on slow processors unless the problem needs it.
If the AI can't come up with a change that checks out, it stops and explains instead of trying again and again, and it no longer repeats the same lookup.

Smarter AI recommendations for every server. Setup measures your server's memory speed in a second or two, combines it with its processor, graphics card and free memory, and recommends the smartest model that works in a reasonable time there, with the reason and the expected time. Usually that's one model: a second is only suggested when it would be clearly faster.

Estimates that learn your server. Every fix measures how fast the model really reads and writes on your server, and corrects the estimates for the other models too, so recommendations and progress times get more accurate the more you use it.
Progress while the AI works counts the whole step (loading, reading and writing), not just reading, so the time left is much closer to reality.
Removing every AI model starts setup again from the beginning, with fresh recommendations.

The AI reads much less before starting, so fixes are faster: logs are boiled down to errors, warnings and the latest lines with repeats merged (a noisy 31,000-character log becomes a few lines), settings files show only the lines around the setting in question, Diagnostics only shows problems, and its own instructions are shorter. The fix for a broken setting now reads about 40% less.
Each AI step shows what it read: its instructions, the problem, and what it looked up.

A guided setup for the built-in AI. The first time you choose Fix with AI, a few short steps walk you through it: pick the AI models (picked for your server), what it may do, what it may look at, and how hard it thinks. The download starts as soon as you pick the models and keeps going while you choose the rest. Change any of it later in Settings → Built-in AI.
Choose what the AI may look at. App logs, files on your server, Activity and Restore, and server details can each be turned off. Passwords, tokens and keys are always hidden from it.

The recommended models download as one pipeline with one progress view: disk space is checked for all of them first, they download one after another (smallest first), and each is checked, loaded into memory and tested while the next one downloads, so everything is ready sooner.

Every step of getting a model ready is shown as it happens, with download speed, time left, which part it's on, loading into memory, and a test that measures how fast it is on your server. Then it starts on your problem as soon as it's ready.
While the AI works, you see each step as it happens: what it looked up, which model is reading and how much, a progress bar with the time left, and how long every step took.

Much faster fixes. Manifexus looks up the obvious things (the file or app in question) before the AI starts, and small file changes are written as a one-line edit instead of the whole file, so a fix like a wrong setting takes one AI round instead of several.

Choose Automatically (in Settings → Built-in AI, on by default). Each problem gets the right model and amount of thinking: simple ones stay quick, tricky ones go to the fixer and think it through, and if the quick helper gets stuck the fixer takes over. The fixer only runs when there's enough free memory at that moment.
The AI's explanations appear all at once when they're ready, nicely formatted: numbered steps, code blocks with a Copy button, tables and highlighted names and paths.
Activity has new Fixes and Fix with AI filters.
fixed: When a fix finishes, a Done button is always there to close it.
No more garbled patches behind a screen while the AI starts up.
Undo Fix no longer says it failed when it actually put the file back.
Fix with AI no longer fails with "fetch failed" after 5 minutes when it takes a long time on a slow processor. If the AI engine really stops responding, you get a plain explanation.
Fix with AI waits until setup is completely finished (every model downloaded, tested and loaded into memory), so the right model can be chosen and nothing else slows it down.
The progress line no longer claims the AI has finished reading when it hasn't. Past the time estimate, it says so and keeps a moving bar.
The AI's look at recent Activity shows the real error messages instead of "[object Object]".
Removing an AI model no longer shows "Unexpected end of JSON input" when it actually worked, and tapping Remove on a model that's already gone isn't an error.
AI fixes no longer stay "In progress" in Activity forever. Each ends as done, failed (with the reason) or stopped.

releases.headline: Meet Ask Manifexus: a private AI, built in, that can look into problems and fix them with your OK.
new: Ask Manifexus. Tap Ask in the header and ask anything about your apps: why something stopped, what changed, what's using the most memory.
It runs on your own server. It's free and private, and nothing leaves your network.
Picked for your server. Manifexus checks your memory, processor and graphics card, and recommends AI models that fit without slowing your apps down.
Downloads that don't give up. If the connection drops, the AI download picks up where it stopped, even after a restart. Every download is checked before it's used.
Fix with AI. One tap from the To Fix list in Diagnostics, and it works out what's wrong.
You're always in control. Every change is shown to you first, with a before and after of every file. It's backed up, and you can undo it from Restore.
Choose how much it may do on its own: Look Only, Ask Before Changes, Fix Routine Things or Expert.
Learn how it's done. Turn on Show Commands (or choose Advanced in Settings) to see the command behind every step, with a plain explanation of each part.
Do It Myself. Every AI fix can be done by hand instead, one step at a time, with the terminal a tap away.
Activity → Commands. A learning log of every command behind your recent changes, and How It Was Done on every activity.
improved: Updates now show version numbers and notes like these, instead of build codes.
Activity has a new Fixes filter.
fixed: On phones, the dashboard no longer shifts sideways by a few pixels.
If an AI model can't download, you get a clear reason and a Try Again button.
Updating Manifexus keeps your settings, history, backups and AI models, even if no data folder was set up. Diagnostics now tells you if one is missing.

releases.headline: The first full release: move, restore and understand your Docker apps, all in one place.
new: Restore. Go back to before any move or delete. Every change keeps a backup, and restores can be undone too.
Activity. A complete record of everything Manifexus does, with the exact reason when something fails.
Diagnostics. Health checks in plain words, with a To Fix list that stays until each issue is fixed.
App Details. Every app's health, resources, storage, network and what it has printed, in one place.
Software updates that restore the previous version automatically if the new one doesn't start.
improved: One clean, consistent design throughout, with every screen the same size.
Settings save as you change them.
fixed: A leftover app entry in one stack can no longer break moving apps into it.
